summary: Carl Gustav Jung worked in religious studies and other fields. He studied at Wilhelmsgymnasium, Pädagogium Basel, and earned a medical degree at the University of Basel (1895–1900). He held posts at the University of Zurich (~1905–1913), ETH Zurich (1933–1942), and Basel (1944).

Carl Olson specializes in religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. Mentored by John Y. Fenton, he served as Teacher-Scholar Chair in the Humanities at Allegheny College (attested 2005–2015).

Carl Paul Caspari was a scholar of religious studies and linguistics. He studied at the University of Leipzig (1834–1842) under Heinrich Leberecht Fleischer and at Humboldt University of Berlin (~1838–1840). He served at the University of Oslo from 1847, becoming professor in 1857.
Carl Schuster was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Sinology. He pursued his studies at Harvard University (~1923–1930) and the University of Vienna (~1932–1934).

Carl Shigeo Yamamoto works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia, where he was supervised by Jeffrey Hopkins and David Germano, and also studied under Sonam Germano, William A. Magee, and Tsering Wangchuk.

Carl Siegfried worked in Indology, linguistics, and religious studies. He studied at Halle-Wittenberg, Bonn, and under Albrecht Weber and Rudolf von Roth. He taught at several gymnasiums, held a Sanskrit professorship at Trinity College Dublin, and was professor at Jena (1875–1901).

Carl W. Ernst works in Indology and religious studies. He earned degrees from Stanford University (~1969–1973) and Harvard University (~1973–1981). He taught at Pomona College (1981–1992) and served as professor at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill (1992–2022).

Carl Wilhelm Vollgraff was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. Educated in Brussels, Utrecht, Göttingen, and Berlin, he studied under Friedrich Leo and Ulrich von Wilamowitz-Moellendorff. He held professorships in Greek at Groningen (1908–1916) and Utrecht (1917–1946).

Carlo Formichi was an Indologist who studied under Michele Kerbaker, Paul Deussen, Hermann Oldenberg, and Georg Bühler, including studies at Kiel University. He served as professor of Sanskrit at the University of Pisa (1898) and Sapienza University of Rome (1914–1941).
Carlo Giussani was a scholar of Indology and linguistics. He studied at the Scuola Normale Superiore (~1859–1863) and was taught by Giuseppe Bardelli, Rudolf von Roth, and Albrecht Weber.
Carlo Jamelle Harris works in philosophy and Buddhist studies. He completed an MA in philosophy at National Chengchi University under the supervision of Chen-kuo Lin (attested 2009).

Carmen Blacker was a scholar of Japanology and religious studies. She studied at SOAS, Somerville College, and Keio University under Shigeru Gorai. She served as a lecturer at the University of Cambridge from 1955 and was president of the Folklore Society (1982–1984).

Carmen Dragonetti worked in Buddhist studies, Indology, and philosophy. She studied at the National University of San Marcos (~1958–1964). She was a professor at the University of Buenos Aires (attested 1989) and vice director of the Instituto de Investigaciones Budistas (~1989–2018).

Carmen Meinert works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Bonn (–2001) and has held posts at the University of Hamburg (attested 2008) and Ruhr University Bochum (attested 2019).
Carol A. Breckenridge worked in Indology, history, and archaeology. She studied at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (~1968–1976) and held a post at the University of Chicago (~1982–1993).

Carol S. Anderson is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under W. S. Karunatillake and John A. Brinkman, and served as Associate Professor of Religion at Kalamazoo College (attested 2004).

Carola Roloff is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar. She studied under Geshe Thubten Ngawang and David P. Jackson, earning a degree at the University of Hamburg. Her posts include visiting professor at the University of Hamburg (2018–2025).
Carola S. Carstens works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. She held a post at Rice University (1998–1999) and earned a doctoral degree from the University of Hamburg (–2006).
Carole M. Cusack is a religious studies scholar. She studied at the University of Sydney from 1988 to 1995 and held a post there in 2013.

Carole McGranahan is a scholar of Tibetology, history, and archaeology. She studied at Colgate University and the University of Michigan, completing her PhD under Nicholas Dirks and Ann Laura Stoler. In ~2001, she joined the University of Colorado Boulder.
